newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE robusta futures end mostly higher on NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE robusta futures end mostly higher on NY.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures recovered from an early slide to end mostly higher on bargain-hunting and reflected the firmer New York trend.
Traders said the August LIFFE certified stock figures released on Monday were low but within trade expectation.
The certifieds fell to 929 five-tonne lots in August from 1,174 lots in July.
"Now we should see coffee starting to come in from Indonesia," said one trader.
By the close, November stood $4 down at $1,530 a tonne but other traded positions were between $1 and $9 higher.
Volume on the exchange reached 2,723 lots.
The market was softer in the morning as the market braced for cheaper coffee from Brazil following the removal of a 13-percent export tax, traders said.
"The passing of the tax has put a lid on buying," said one trader on Monday.
The Brazilian Senate last week approved a bill to scratch the coffee export tax, paving the way for cheaper exports, said traders.
The market recovered on bargain hunting in the afternoon "...but its New York which is leading us all the way," one said.
"New York wants to consolidate," said another trader.
The London Commodity Exchange is now trading under the London International Financial Futures (LIFFE) banner after a landmark merger on Monday.
But traders said the merger was largely cosmetic so far and fundamental changes were only expected once the commodity and financial futures were housed under the same roof.
